title: Conditional probability and Bayes
explanation:
$P(A\mid B)$ is the probability that $A$ happens given that $B$ has already happened [1]. The condition **shrinks the world**: a conditional reduces the sample space [2] to just the outcomes where $B$ is true, and we ask what fraction of those also have $A$. So $P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$.

Bayes' theorem turns a conditional around. In medical testing it computes the chance of disease given a positive test, using how prevalent the disease is and how well the test works [3]. The cleanest way to feel it is with **natural frequencies**: imagine 1000 people, split them by disease status, then by test result, and count.

Direction matters. As Wikipedia's example warns, if all patients with a disease show a symptom, it does not follow that everyone with the symptom has the disease [4]. $P(+\mid D)$ and $P(D\mid +)$ can be very different, especially when the disease is rare.
keyIdeas: $P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$: restrict to the world where $B$ happened.
Bayes combines prevalence (prior) with test accuracy.
Natural frequencies (imagine 1000 people) make Bayes problems countable.

workedExample.problem: A condition affects $2\%$ of people. A test catches $90\%$ of cases and gives a false positive for $5\%$ of healthy people. If someone tests positive, how likely are they to have the condition?
steps: Imagine 1000 people: 20 have the condition, 980 do not.
Restrict to the positives: $18+49=67$ people, of whom 18 have the condition.
workedExample.answer: $\frac{18}{67}\approx0.27$, far lower than the test's $90\%$ hit rate

pitfalls: Ignoring the base rate: a rare condition means many positives are false.
Dividing by the whole population instead of by the size of the conditioning group.

citations.quote: P ( A | B ) is the probability that event A will occur given that the event B has already occurred.
A conditional reduces the sample space.
using quantities that specify how prevalent the disease is in the population and how well the test works
For example, if all patients with pancreatic cancer have certain symptoms, it does not follow that anyone who has those symptoms has pancreatic cancer.
